tasks.title: Project Setup & Core Design System Implementation
tasks.description: Initialize the project repository, set up the development environment, and implement the foundational design system components based on the PRD's brand identity and visual design specifications.
tasks.details: Establish responsive breakpoints (mobile: 320-768px, tablet: 768-1024px, desktop: 1024px+, large desktop: 1440px+). Define and implement the primary color palette (#000000, #DC143C, #D4AF37) and secondary colors (#36454F, #C0C0C0). Implement typography styles using Cinzel for display, a clean sans-serif for body, and monospace for technical details. Develop initial component library elements such as navigation structure, buttons (multiple styles), and basic card layouts.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify color accuracy and typography application across various elements. Test responsiveness of initial components on different screen sizes. Ensure component library is well-structured and reusable.

subtasks.title: Project Initialization & Boilerplate Cleanup
subtasks.description: Initialize the Git repository, ensure the Vite development environment is functional, and remove or refactor the default Vite + React boilerplate code to prepare for new development. This includes cleaning up `App.tsx`, `App.css`, and `HelloWorld.tsx`.
subtasks.details:
1. Initialize Git repository if not already done.
2. Verify `npm install` and `npm run dev` work correctly.
3. Remove `src/assets` directory and its contents (react.svg, vite.svg).
4. Clean up `src/App.tsx` to a minimal functional component (e.g., just rendering a `div` with 'Cursed Ink Society').
5. Clean up `src/App.css` to remove boilerplate styles.
6. Remove `src/components/HelloWorld.tsx` and its import from `App.tsx`.
7. Update `src/index.css` to remove any boilerplate styles not related to the new design system.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run dev` and verify the application loads with a minimal, clean output. Ensure no console errors related to removed files.

subtasks.title: Implement Design Tokens (Colors & Typography)
subtasks.description: Define and implement the project's primary and secondary color palettes and typography styles as CSS variables in `src/index.css`. This includes importing custom fonts.
subtasks.details:
1. Define CSS variables for primary colors (`--color-primary-black`, `--color-primary-red`, `--color-primary-gold`) using #000000, #DC143C, #D4AF37.
2. Define CSS variables for secondary colors (`--color-secondary-charcoal`, `--color-secondary-silver`) using #36454F, #C0C0C0.
3. Import Cinzel font for display, a clean sans-serif (e.g., Inter, or another suitable Google Font) for body, and a monospace font (e.g., Fira Code, or another suitable Google Font) for technical details. Ensure fonts are loaded efficiently.
4. Define CSS variables for font families (`--font-family-display`, `--font-family-body`, `--font-family-monospace`).
5. Apply `--font-family-body` to the `body` element in `src/index.css`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Inspect elements in the browser developer tools to verify that the new CSS variables for colors and fonts are correctly defined in `:root` and applied. Create a simple test page or modify `App.tsx` temporarily to display text with different font families and colored elements to visually confirm.

subtasks.title: Establish Responsive Breakpoints & Global Styles
subtasks.description: Define responsive breakpoints using CSS media queries and establish foundational global responsive styles in `src/index.css`.
subtasks.details:
1. Define CSS variables for breakpoint values (e.g., `--breakpoint-mobile-max`, `--breakpoint-tablet-min`, etc.) in `src/index.css`.
2. Implement media queries for mobile (320-768px), tablet (768-1024px), desktop (1024px+), and large desktop (1440px+).
3. Add basic responsive adjustments to `body` or a main container (e.g., `max-width`, `padding`) within these media queries to ensure content adapts.
4. Ensure `min-width: 320px` is set on `body` or `html`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Resize the browser window to verify that the defined media queries trigger at the correct screen widths. Use developer tools to inspect styles applied at different breakpoints.

subtasks.title: Develop Core UI Components (Buttons & Cards)
subtasks.description: Create reusable React components for buttons (multiple styles) and a basic card layout, applying the newly defined design tokens.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a `src/components/Button/Button.tsx` component.
2. Define CSS for button styles (e.g., `primary`, `secondary`, `outline`) in `src/components/Button/Button.module.css` (using CSS Modules for component-specific styles).
3. Ensure buttons use the new color and typography design tokens.
4. Create a `src/components/Card/Card.tsx` component.
5. Define CSS for basic card styles (e.g., padding, border, background) in `src/components/Card/Card.module.css`.
6. Ensure cards use the new color design tokens.
7. Update `App.tsx` to demonstrate usage of these new components.
subtasks.testStrategy: Render instances of each button style and card in `App.tsx`. Visually inspect them to ensure they match the design specifications (colors, fonts, spacing). Test button hover/active states. Verify responsiveness of cards.

subtasks.title: Develop Navigation Structure Component
subtasks.description: Create a foundational React component for the website's main navigation structure, incorporating responsiveness and applying design tokens.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a `src/components/Navigation/Navigation.tsx` component.
2. Define CSS for the navigation bar (e.g., background, text color, spacing) in `src/components/Navigation/Navigation.module.css`.
3. Include placeholder navigation links (e.g., Home, Artists, Services, Contact).
4. Implement basic responsiveness for the navigation (e.g., stacking links on mobile, or a simple hamburger menu placeholder).
5. Ensure the navigation uses the new color and typography design tokens.
6. Integrate the `Navigation` component into `App.tsx`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Render the navigation component in `App.tsx`. Visually inspect its appearance and responsiveness across different screen sizes. Ensure placeholder links are styled correctly.

tasks.title: Develop Homepage (/)
tasks.description: Create the main landing page for the website, incorporating the hero section, artist spotlight, portfolio preview, services overview, and primary calls-to-action.
tasks.details: Design and implement a dramatic hero section with compelling headline and imagery. Integrate a rotating featured artists section. Showcase a high-quality portfolio preview. Provide an overview of premium services. Include clear calls-to-action for contact and social proof elements. Ensure dark, moody aesthetic with high-contrast imagery.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify all sections are present and visually align with brand identity. Test responsiveness across devices. Ensure CTAs are functional and lead to correct pages. Check image loading and display.

tasks.title: Implement Artist Profiles & Listing (/artists)
tasks.description: Develop the main artist listing page and individual artist profile pages, including their specialties, social media, and portfolio integration.
tasks.details: Create a dedicated '/artists' page listing all artists. For each artist (Anthony Boudreaux, Ashley Wood, Cody Crochet, Seth Wood, Luis Reymundo, Trent), create an individual profile page. Each profile must include their specialty, style, personality, key message, social media links (e.g., @buddha_ta2 for Anthony), and integrate their specific work galleries. Ensure booking information/contact methods are clearly displayed.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify all artists are listed and their individual profile pages are accessible. Check that social media links are correct and functional. Ensure portfolio integration is ready for content. Test responsiveness of artist cards and profiles.

subtasks.title: Define Artist Data Structure and Initial Data Population
subtasks.description: Create or refine `src/data/artistsData.js` to hold comprehensive information for all specified artists (Anthony Boudreaux, Ashley Wood, Cody Crochet, Seth Wood, Luis Reymundo, Trent).
subtasks.details: This data will serve as the single source of truth for all artist-related content across the site. Include fields for `id`, `name`, `specialty`, `style`, `personality`, `keyMessage`, `social` (e.g., `instagram`, `facebook`), `contact` (email/phone), and `gallery` (array of image objects with `src`, `alt`). Populate with placeholder data for all artists. Ensure image paths are structured for easy integration later (e.g., `/images/artists/anthony/tattoo1.jpg`).
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify `src/data/artistsData.js` exists and contains well-structured objects for all 6 artists with all required fields populated with placeholder data.

subtasks.title: Develop Artist Listing Page Component (`/artists`)
subtasks.description: Create `src/pages/ArtistListPage.jsx` and `src/styles/components/_artistListPage.scss`. This page will fetch data from `artistsData.js` and display a grid or list of `ArtistCard` components.
subtasks.details: Each `ArtistCard` should be a reusable component displaying the artist's name, specialty, and a thumbnail image, linking to their individual profile page. Design the layout to be responsive and visually align with the dark, moody aesthetic.
subtasks.testStrategy: Navigate to `/artists`. Verify all 6 artists are displayed with their name, specialty, and a placeholder image. Ensure each artist card is clickable and visually distinct.

subtasks.title: Create Individual Artist Profile Page Component (`/artists/:id`)
subtasks.description: Create `src/pages/ArtistProfilePage.jsx` and `src/styles/components/_artistProfilePage.scss`. This component will dynamically load artist data based on the URL parameter (`:id`).
subtasks.details: Implement logic to retrieve the correct artist object from `artistsData.js` using `useParams` from `react-router-dom`. The page must display the artist's name, specialty, style, personality, key message, social media links, booking information (email/phone), and a section for their portfolio gallery. Structure the page clearly with distinct sections for bio, social, and portfolio.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manually navigate to `/artists/anthony-boudreaux` (and other artist IDs). Verify that the correct artist's details are displayed, including all specified text fields and contact information.

subtasks.title: Implement Portfolio Gallery and Social Media Link Integration
subtasks.description: Within `ArtistProfilePage.jsx`, develop a dedicated section to display the artist's portfolio images and integrate clickable social media links.
subtasks.details: Create a `Gallery` component (e.g., `src/components/Gallery.jsx`) to display multiple images from the artist's `gallery` array in a visually appealing grid or carousel. Implement clickable social media icons/links for Instagram and Facebook, pulling data from the `social` field in `artistsData.js`. Ensure social media links open in a new tab.
subtasks.testStrategy: On an artist's profile page, verify that placeholder gallery images are displayed correctly within the portfolio section. Click on social media links to ensure they open the correct (even if placeholder) URLs in new tabs.

subtasks.title: Configure React Router for Artist Routes
subtasks.description: Update `src/App.js` to include the new routes for the artist listing page and individual artist profile pages.
subtasks.details: Use `react-router-dom`'s `Routes` and `Route` components. The main listing page should be accessible at `/artists`, and individual profiles at `/artists/:id`. Ensure the dynamic route for individual profiles is correctly configured to capture the artist ID.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify direct navigation to `/artists` works. From the `/artists` page, click on an artist card to ensure it navigates correctly to the corresponding individual profile page (e.g., `/artists/anthony-boudreaux`). Test invalid IDs to ensure a graceful fallback (e.g., 404 or redirect).

tasks.title: Build Portfolio/Gallery System (/gallery)
tasks.description: Create a robust and performant portfolio/gallery system with advanced filtering, search, and high-resolution image display.
tasks.details: Implement an advanced filtering system by artist, style, and body placement. Ensure high-resolution images are displayed with professional photography standards. Include a search functionality for specific styles or artists. Optimize for fast-loading image galleries using lazy loading. Consider 'before/after' views if applicable for future content.
tasks.testStrategy: Test all filtering and search functionalities for accuracy and performance. Verify image quality and loading speed. Check lazy loading implementation. Ensure gallery navigation is smooth and intuitive.

subtasks.title: Establish Gallery Page Structure and Mock Data Integration
subtasks.description: Create the `/gallery` route, the main `GalleryPage` component, and define a mock data structure for gallery items (including artist, style, body placement, image URLs, etc.). Integrate this mock data into the page for initial display.
subtasks.details: Create `src/pages/GalleryPage.jsx` (or .tsx), add route to `src/App.jsx` (or router configuration). Define `src/data/galleryData.json` or `src/api/mockGallery.js` with sample tattoo entries, ensuring fields for artist, style, and body placement are present. The structure should align with future backend data models.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify `/gallery` route loads the `GalleryPage` component. Confirm mock data is accessible and can be rendered (e.g., console.log or basic list display).

subtasks.title: Develop Gallery Image Grid and Implement Lazy Loading
subtasks.description: Design and implement the visual grid layout for gallery images. Integrate a lazy loading mechanism for all images within the gallery to optimize initial page load performance, adhering to principles from Task 8.
subtasks.details: Create `src/components/GalleryGrid/GalleryGrid.jsx` and `src/components/GalleryCard/GalleryCard.jsx`. Utilize `IntersectionObserver` API or a lightweight lazy loading library (e.g., `react-lazyload`) to ensure images only load when they enter the viewport. Implement image placeholders or low-resolution previews.
subtasks.testStrategy: Visually inspect image grid layout for proper alignment and responsiveness. Use browser developer tools (Network tab) to confirm images load only as they become visible on screen. Check for smooth scrolling performance.

subtasks.title: Implement Advanced Filtering UI and Logic
subtasks.description: Develop interactive UI components (e.g., dropdowns, checkboxes) for filtering gallery items by artist, style, and body placement. Implement the client-side logic to filter the displayed images based on user selections.
subtasks.details: Create `src/components/GalleryFilters/GalleryFilters.jsx`. Implement state management for filter selections (e.g., using React hooks or Redux). Apply filtering logic to the gallery data before rendering, ensuring multiple filters can be combined. Consider dynamic population of filter options from the mock data.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test each filter independently (artist, style, body placement). Verify that only relevant images are displayed after applying filters. Test combinations of filters. Check filter reset functionality.

subtasks.title: Integrate Search Functionality and High-Resolution Image Viewer
subtasks.description: Add a search input field to the gallery page, allowing users to search for specific styles or artists. Implement the search logic to dynamically update the displayed gallery. Additionally, create a high-resolution image viewer (e.g., a modal/lightbox) that displays the full-quality image when a gallery item is clicked.
subtasks.details: Create `src/components/GallerySearch/GallerySearch.jsx` and `src/components/ImageViewer/ImageViewer.jsx`. Ensure search functionality works in conjunction with active filters. The image viewer should support displaying high-resolution images and potentially offer basic navigation (next/previous) within the gallery context.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test search with various keywords (artist names, styles). Verify search results are accurate and update dynamically. Click on gallery images to ensure the high-resolution viewer opens correctly and displays the full image. Test navigation within the viewer if implemented.

subtasks.title: Refine UI/UX, Ensure Responsiveness, and Final Integration
subtasks.description: Apply the established design system (Task 1) to all gallery components, ensuring consistent styling, typography, and color palette. Optimize the gallery layout and components for responsiveness across all defined breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop, large desktop). Conduct a final integration pass to ensure all features (filtering, search, lazy loading, image viewer) work seamlessly together.
subtasks.details: Review all CSS/styling for adherence to Task 1's design system (colors, typography, spacing). Implement media queries or use responsive component patterns to ensure optimal display on mobile, tablet, and desktop. Perform cross-browser compatibility checks. Ensure smooth transitions and interactions.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manually test responsiveness on various screen sizes/device emulators (e.g., Chrome DevTools device mode). Verify all interactive elements (filters, search, image clicks) function correctly after styling. Check overall performance and visual appeal across different browsers. Ensure Core Web Vitals are not negatively impacted.

tasks.title: Develop Services Page (/services) & Aftercare Content
tasks.description: Create a comprehensive services page detailing tattoo types, pricing structure, process explanation, and essential aftercare information.
tasks.details: Categorize services (tattoo types, sizes, complexity). Provide clear pricing transparency. Explain the consultation and tattooing process. Include comprehensive aftercare guidance. Showcase safety and hygiene standards. Integrate relevant visual style elements.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify all service categories and information are present and accurate. Check clarity of pricing and process explanations. Ensure aftercare information is easily accessible and readable. Test responsiveness of the page layout.

tasks.title: Create About Us (/about) & Contact Pages (/contact)
tasks.description: Develop the 'About Us' page to convey the studio's story and team, and the 'Contact' page with multiple contact methods, a professional inquiry form, and map integration.
tasks.details: For the '/about' page: tell Cursed Ink Society's mission and vision, introduce the artist collective, showcase the professional studio environment, highlight community values, and articulate the brand philosophy. For the '/contact' page: include multiple contact methods (phone, email, social media links), a professional contact form with secure submissions, studio address and hours, and map integration for location visualization.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify all information on the 'About Us' page is accurate and engaging. Test all contact methods on the 'Contact' page, including form submission and map functionality. Ensure secure form submissions.

tasks.title: Implement Advanced Features (Social Media & CMS Integration)
tasks.description: Integrate social media feeds and establish the foundation for a content management system to allow for easy updates of artist profiles and portfolio images.
tasks.details: Implement Instagram feed integration on relevant pages (e.g., artist profiles, homepage). Ensure social media links are present for each artist and the main collective. Implement share functionality for portfolio pieces. Develop backend capabilities for easy artist profile updates and portfolio image management, laying groundwork for content scheduling and SEO optimization tools.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify Instagram feeds are pulling correctly and social links are functional. Test share functionality. Confirm that content update mechanisms are in place and accessible for future content managers.

tasks.title: Performance & Mobile Optimization
tasks.description: Optimize the entire website for superior performance, mobile-first responsiveness, and Core Web Vitals compliance.
tasks.details: Achieve page load times under 3 seconds on both mobile and desktop. Ensure all Core Web Vitals metrics are in the 'Good' range. Implement 100% mobile-first responsive design across all pages. Conduct comprehensive image optimization, lazy loading for all media, and efficient code splitting.
tasks.testStrategy: Use Lighthouse and other performance tools to verify load times and Core Web Vitals scores (aim for 90+). Manually test responsiveness on various mobile and tablet devices. Check for smooth scrolling and interactive elements on all screen sizes.

tasks.title: SEO & Accessibility Implementation
tasks.description: Implement comprehensive SEO strategies to improve search rankings and ensure full WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance.
tasks.details: Apply local SEO targeting for Houma, Louisiana. Implement technical SEO elements including schema markup, meta tags, and sitemaps. Optimize content for relevant tattoo service keywords. Ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, including screen reader support, full keyboard navigation, sufficient color contrast, and comprehensive alt text for all images.
tasks.testStrategy: Conduct technical SEO audits to verify meta tags, schema, and sitemap. Use accessibility testing tools (e.g., Axe, Lighthouse Accessibility) and manual screen reader tests to ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. Verify keyboard navigation throughout the site.

tasks.title: Testing, Validation & Deployment Preparation
tasks.description: Conduct thorough testing across all implemented features, validate against PRD requirements, and prepare the website for production deployment.
tasks.details: Perform cross-browser compatibility testing (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari). Conduct functional testing of all forms, links, and interactive elements. Execute performance and accessibility audits. Implement security checks (SSL certificate, secure forms, data protection). Prepare deployment scripts and documentation for a smooth launch.
tasks.testStrategy: Run comprehensive end-to-end tests. Verify all success metrics from the PRD are met (e.g., bounce rate, session duration, contact form completion). Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) if possible. Ensure all security measures are in place and validated.
